newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon peacekeepers say shepherd killed in blast.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon peacekeepers say shepherd killed in blast.

text.p: A Lebanese shepherd was killed on Thursday in a land mine blast in his south Lebanon village, Lebanese security sources said.
The sources said Khodr Shehadeh, 23, was killed when he stepped over a land mine planted in the village of Froun just north of a south Lebanon zone occupied by Israeli forces.
It was not immediately known who planted the land mine.
Officers at the U.N. Interim Forces in Lebanon told Reuters that the Finnish batallion operating in the area heard an explosion and sent a patrol to the site.
"We are investigating the cause of the blast," a UNIFIL spokesman said.
Lebanese security sources had previously said the killing was a result of Israeli shelling but the Israeli army denied the report.

Sources with the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militia (SLA), which patrols the zone, said guerrillas fired mortar bombs and anti-tank rockets at a post manned by the militiamen at Shoumariyeh on the edge of the zone facing Froun.

"After checks, we found it impossible a Lebanese citizen could have been hit by fire which Israeli army forces shot in response to terrorist fire that was directed towards an SLA outpost," an Israeli military spokeswoman said.
"The Israeli army returned artillery fire only towards the sources of fire and we emphasise nothing was shot in the area of Froun village," she said.
In reply to a question, the spokeswoman also denied the SLA had fired towards Froun.
UNIFIL sources said a five-nation committee monitoring a U.S.-brokered south Lebanon ceasefire agreement would meet on Friday to mull a Lebanese complaint over the killing of the shepherd.

The committee comprising the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel unanimously condemned on Wednesday the Israeli shelling of February 18 which killed a civilian woman and wounded two others in south Lebanon.
Under the April 26 U.S.-sponsored understanding, Israel and Hizbollah are barred from targeting civilians.

The pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war on Israeli and SLA forces in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine-miles) -deep south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to prevent cross-border attacks on northern Israel.
